name: MMKV
verdict_reason: Tencent's chart shows a large write advantage over NSUserDefaults for 10,000 writes, but the page itself says reads only equal or exceed NSUserDefaults, the figures exist only as chart labels, and the run is on iOS 13.3.1.
tier_reason: First-party results that appear only in a chart image; the page text is directional.
claimed_speedup: Text: MMKV beats NSUserDefaults on writes and 'equals or outranges NSUserDefaults on reading values', each operation repeated 1w (10,000) times; the README's chart covers 'Writing random `int` for 10000 times'. Values appear only in the chart image.
workload: 10,000 sequential writes, then reads, of random ints and of strings under distinct keys in the MMKVDemo app; the NSUserDefaults write loop calls synchronize once at the end.
platforms: iOS, macOS, Android, Windows, POSIX, HarmonyOS NEXT
one_liner: mmap-backed key-value store from WeChat; much faster than NSUserDefaults for bulk writes in a vendor chart, on par for reads.
how_it_is_fast: MMKV memory-maps its file, so a write is an append into mapped memory that the kernel flushes later, with no round trip to the cfprefsd daemon and no property-list re-serialization. Values are protobuf-encoded and appended; the file is rewritten only when it fills and needs compaction.
use_it_when: Many small writes in loops or on hot paths, where NSUserDefaults' per-write cost dominates
Sharing key-value data between an app and its extensions with MMKV's multi-process mode
skip_it_when: Read-mostly settings: reads are published as on par with NSUserDefaults
You need Settings.bundle, @AppStorage, key-value observation or managed app configuration, which are tied to UserDefaults
caveats: Numbers exist only in a chart image; read from its labels (not page text): write int 8 vs 3728.5 ms, write string 17.75 vs 4247.75 ms, read int 1.5 vs 9 ms, read string 3.5 vs 8.25 ms
iOS 13.3.1 on an iPhone 11 Pro Max; no newer iOS measurement found
Benchmark date not stated; build configuration not stated
Vendor benchmark of a sequential microbenchmark; real apps rarely write 10,000 keys in a row
tradeoffs: Adds a C++ library to the app
Data in mapped pages that the kernel has not flushed can be lost on sudden power loss
GitHub does not detect the license (NOASSERTION); the license file combines Tencent's BSD 3-Clause terms with notices for bundled code
